facts.statement: Saurornithoides lived during the Late Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Late Cretaceous

facts.statement: The first fossils of Saurornithoides were discovered on July 9, 1923, by a Chinese employee of an American Museum of Natural History expedition.
facts.quote: The fossils were found on 9 July 1923 by a Chinese employee of an American Museum of Natural History expedition, Chih.

facts.statement: Henry Fairfield Osborn initially intended to name the animal "Ornithoides" but published the name in 1924 without a formal description, making it an invalid nomen nudum.
facts.quote: Henry Fairfield Osborn at first intended to name the animal "Ornithoides", the "bird-like one", and in 1924 mentioned this name in a popular publication but without a description so that it remained an invalid nomen nudum.

facts.statement: The generic name Saurornithoides translates to "saurian with bird-like rostrum" and was chosen because of the taxon's bird-like bones.
facts.quote: The generic name was chosen because of the bird-like bones of the taxon, which was thought to represent a megalosaurian, translating as "saurian with bird-like rostrum".

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Saurornithoides is cataloged as AMNH 6516.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen is AMNH 6516.

facts.statement: In 1964, a second specimen (IGM 100/1), the first collected by a professional Mongolian paleontologist, was described from the Late Cretaceous of Mongolia.
facts.quote: In 1964, another specimen was described from the Late Cretaceous of Mongolia. The first specimen ever collected by a professional Mongolian palaeontologist, it was given the specimen number IGM 100/1.

facts.statement: A 2009 study reassigned Saurornithoides junior to its own genus, Zanabazar, due to the description of many more troodontids with cranial material.
facts.quote: However, since the description, many more troodontids have been described with cranial material, and as such, a 2009 study on Saurornithoides reassigned this species to its own genus, Zanabazar.

facts.statement: A juvenile specimen of S. mongoliensis was described in 1993.
facts.quote: In 1993, a juvenile specimen of S. mongoliensis was described.

facts.statement: Baron Franz Nopcsa coined the name Saurornithoides sauvagei in 1928, but this was a result of a printing error intended for Teinurosaurus sauvagei.
facts.quote: In 1928, baron Franz Nopcsa coined Saurornithoides sauvagei. However, this was the result of a printing error: he had planned to name a Teinurosaurus sauvagei.

facts.statement: Kenneth Carpenter renamed Stenonychosaurus inequalis to Saurornithoides inequalis in 1982.
facts.quote: In 1982, Kenneth Carpenter renamed Stenonychosaurus inequalis Sternberg 1932 into Saurornithoides inequalis.

facts.statement: George Olshevsky renamed Pectinodon asiamericanus to Saurornithoides asiamericanus in 1991.
facts.quote: In 1991, George Olshevsky renamed Pectinodon asiamericanus Nesov 1985 into Saurornithoides asiamericanus.

facts.statement: George Olshevsky renamed Troodon isfarensis to Saurornithoides isfarensis in 2000.
facts.quote: In 2000, Olshevsky renamed Troodon isfarensis Nessov 1995 into Saurornithoides isfarensis.

facts.statement: In 2007, it was determined that Saurornithoides isfarensis was actually a hadrosaurid fossil.
facts.quote: In 2007, this was shown to have been a hadrosaurid fossil.

facts.statement: Saurornithoides were predators capable of running fast on their hind legs with excellent sight and hearing.
facts.quote: These creatures were predators, which could run fast on their hind legs and had excellent sight and hearing.

facts.statement: The name Saurornithoides is derived from Greek stems meaning lizard, bird, and form, referring to its bird-like skull.
facts.quote: The name is derived from the Greek stems saur~ (lizard), ornith~ (bird) and eides (form), referring to its bird-like skull.

facts.statement: Saurornithoides lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 75 million years ago in the Campanian stage, in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 75 million years ago, en el Campaniense, en lo que hoy es Asia.

facts.statement: The name Saurornithoides comes from Greek terms for lizard, bird, and form, fitting for a creature close to the origin of birds.
facts.quote: El nombre se deriva de los términos del griego sauros "lagarto", ornithos "pájaro" y de oides "forma", un nombre apropiado para una criatura cercana al origen de las aves.

facts.statement: Osborn initially classified Saurornithoides in the Megalosauridae due to its resemblance to Velociraptor.
facts.quote: Osborn at first placed Saurornithoides in the Megalosauridae, noticing the resemblance to Velociraptor, named in the same paper.

facts.statement: In 1974, Barsbold recognized the connection between Saurornithoides and American forms like Stenonychosaurus and named the family Saurornithoididae.
facts.quote: Only in 1974, Barsbold, while describing S. junior, understood the connection with American forms such as Stenonychosaurus and named an encompassing Saurornithoididae.

facts.statement: In 1987, Philip John Currie showed that Saurornithoididae was a junior synonym of Troodontidae, confirming Saurornithoides as a troodontid.
facts.quote: In 1987, Philip John Currie showed that this concept was a junior synonym of Troodontidae, implying that Saurornithoides were a troodontid too.

facts.statement: Saurornithoides belongs to the family Troodontidae.
facts.quote: familia: Troodontidae

facts.statement: Saurornithoides was a small troodontid with a type specimen skull length of 189 millimeters, compared to 272 millimeters for the larger Zanabazar junior.
facts.quote: Saurornithoides was a rather small troodontid. Though a possible adult, the type specimen has a midline skull length of 189 millimetres, compared to 272 millimetres for Zanabazar junior, itself estimated at 2.3 meters long.

facts.statement: Saurornithoides likely scoured the Gobi Desert for small mammals or reptiles to eat.
facts.quote: Swift and smart, like its North American cousin Troodon, Saurornithoides probably scoured the Gobi Desert, looking for small mammals or reptiles to eat.

facts.statement: The highly ossified hindlimb of juvenile Saurornithoides suggests they were well developed at birth and required little to no parental care.
facts.quote: the highly ossified hindlimb suggested that Saurornithoides and other troodontids were well developed at birth and that they probably required little to no parental care.

facts.statement: Saurornithoides was a member of the troodontids, a group of small, graceful maniraptorans similar to birds.
facts.quote: Saurornithoides es un miembro de los troodóntidos, un grupo de pequeños y gráciles maniraptores, similares a las aves.

facts.statement: Saurornithoides reached a length of 160 centimeters.
facts.quote: Saurornithoides llegó a medir 160 centímetros de longitud.

facts.statement: It possessed a long, low head, a depressed snout, sharp teeth, and a relatively large brain.
facts.quote: Tenía una cabeza larga y baja, un hocico deprimido, dientes afilados y un cerebro relativamente grande.

facts.statement: Likely fast and intelligent, it probably roamed the Gobi Desert hunting small mammals and reptiles.
facts.quote: Rápido e inteligente, como su primo norteamericano Troodon, Saurornithoides probablemente recorrió el Desierto de Gobi, buscando pequeños mamíferos y reptiles para comer.

facts.statement: The genus was named by paleontologist Osborn in 1924.
facts.quote: Saurornithoides fue nombrado por el paleontólogo Osborn en 1924.

facts.statement: Fossils were found on July 9, 1923, by a Chinese employee of the American Museum of Natural History expedition named Chih.
facts.quote: Los fósiles fueron encontrados el 9 de julio de 1923 por un empleado chino de una expedición del Museo Americano de Historia Natural, Chih.

facts.statement: Only one, possibly two, specimens of this theropod have been found in the Djadokhta Formation of Mongolia.
facts.quote: Uno solo espécimen, posiblemente dos, de este terópodo ha sido encontrado en la Formación Djadochta de Mongolia.

facts.statement: The holotype is specimen AMNH 6516.
facts.quote: El holotipo es la muestra AMNH 6516.

facts.statement: Another specimen from the Late Cretaceous of Mongolia was described in 1964.
facts.quote: En 1964, se describió otro espécimen del Cretácico Superior de Mongolia.

facts.statement: In 2000, Olshevsky renamed Troodon isfarensis Nessov 1995 to Saurornithoides isfarensis.
facts.quote: En 2000, Olshevsky cambió el nombre de Troodon isfarensis Nessov 1995 a Saurornithoides isfarensis.

facts.statement: In 2007, it was demonstrated to be a hadrosaurid fossil.
facts.quote: En 2007, se demostró que era un fósil de hadrosáurido.

facts.statement: In 1987, Philip John Currie demonstrated that the concept was a modern synonym of Troodontidae, implying Saurornithoides was also a troodontid.
facts.quote: En 1987, Philip John Currie demostró que este concepto era un sinónimo más moderno de Troodontidae, lo que implica que Saurornithoides también era un troodóntido.

facts.statement: Its family is Troodontidae.
facts.quote: Family: Troodontidae

facts.statement: It lived from the Cenomanian to the Maastrichtian, between 100.5 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Cenomanian to Maastrichtian (100.5 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Highly ossified hind limbs suggested that Saurornithoides and other troodontids were well-developed at birth and likely required little or no parental care.
facts.quote: La extremidad trasera altamente osificada sugirió que Saurornithoides y otros troodóntidos estaban bien desarrollados al nacer y que probablemente requirieron poco o ningún cuidado de los padres.

facts.statement: A 2009 review found support for linking S. junior to S. mongoliensis to be erroneous, reclassifying it as Zanabazar junior while keeping the species name.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, una revisión de 2009 de este género encontró que el soporte para esta idea era erróneo, siendo reclasificado y S. junior es el nuevo Zanabazar junior, manteniendo el nombre de la especie.

facts.statement: Due to its origin in the Cenomanian of Uzbekistan, it is generally viewed as a different taxon from Saurornithoides.
facts.quote: En vista de su procedencia del Cenomaniano de Uzbekistán, generalmente se lo ve como un taxón diferente de Saurornithoides.
